author: DamiLee
description:
He swore he'd never watch. Then the crowd erupted, and everything changed.

The Colosseum wasn't just a stadium. It was a psychological device built to control the emotions of 50,000 people at once, turning fear into entertainment and violence into spectacle.

A Roman man named Alypius walked in convinced he was above it all. He kept his eyes closed at first. Then the roar hit him.

Saint Augustine wrote that he was "suddenly intoxicated with the joy of blood," shouting with the crowd like everyone else.

The architecture, the noise, the mass of bodies, it was all engineered. Not by accident. By design.

If you think you'd be immune, that's exactly what Alypius thought too.

title: How the Colosseum Games Intoxicated This Man
